simple.meaning: מַשָּׁא (mashshâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a loan ; by implication, interest on a debt.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Nehemiah, beginning at Nehemiah 5:7. The surrounding contexts include family.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַשָּׁא (H4855) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מַשָּׁא (mashshâʼ) / H4855 is traced through Nehemiah 5:7, Nehemiah 5:10, Nehemiah 10:32 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: a loan ; by implication, interest on a debt

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the rulers, and said to them, “You exact usury, everyone of his brother.” I held a great assembly against them.

timeline.evidenceText: Then I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the rulers, and said to them, “You exact usury, everyone of his brother.” I held a great assembly against them.
I likewise, my brothers and my servants, lend them money and grain. Please let us stop this usury.
Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel* A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. for the service of the house of our God;
